newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo Jan/Feb trade deficit $351 million - Tanjug.
newsitem.headline: Yugo Jan/Feb trade deficit $351 million - Tanjug.

text.p: Yugoslavia's trade deficit in the first two months of 1997 stood at $351 million, state news agency Tanjug reported on Tuesday.

"Foreign trade stood at $917 million in the first two months of this year, with exports standing at $283 million and imports at $634 million," Tanjug quoted the director of the Federal statistics office Milovan Zivkovic as saying.
In January the trade gap was $191 with imports accounting for $323 million and exports for $132 million.
According to Zivkovic in the first two months this year exports went up by 48.9 percent and imports by 43.3 percent on the same period last year.
Reproduction material accounted for 69.7 percent, or $422 million of Yugoslavia's imports in the first two months this year and 64 percent, or $181 million, of its exports, Zivkovic said.

"The deficit is the result of the Yugoslav industry's need for imported raw materials and semi-manufactures which should secure an increase in production and exports, ultimately leading to reduction of the trade deficit," Zivkovic said.
European countries are Yugoslavia's main trading parters, accounting for 85 percent of the trade, including Italy, Macedonia, Germany and the Russian Federation, Zivkovic said.
Most of the goods Yugoslavia imported in the first two months were from Germany and the Russian federation, $76 million worth of goods each, he said.
Italy was Yugoslavia's top exporting country, to which it exported $31 million worth of goods in the period.

In February, exports were $139 million, up by 42.8 percent on the same month in 1996, and imports stood at $252 million, up 18 percent on the same month last year. -- Beti Bilandzic, Belgrade newsroom, 381 11 222 43 05
